---
title: "Reactivity and reactive()"
subtitle: "Don't repeat yourself"
---

## The problem: the same code, twice

This is the app of [`apps/02-datasets`](https://github.com/ottaviae/stat-shiny/tree/main/apps/02-datasets): one input, two outputs.

```{shinylive-r}
#| standalone: true
#| components: [editor, viewer]
#| layout: vertical
#| viewerHeight: 650
## file: ui.R
{{< include ../apps/02-datasets/ui.R >}}
## file: server.R
{{< include ../apps/02-datasets/server.R >}}
```

It works, but look at the server: the `switch()` that picks the dataset is written **twice**, once in each `render*()`.

- If you add a dataset, you must remember to change it in **two places**
- Every time the input changes, the same data are prepared **twice**: with a big file or a slow computation, the app becomes slow

## The solution: `reactive()`

`reactive()` creates a **reactive expression**: a recipe that *returns a value* and that the outputs can share.

```r
server <- function(input, output, session) {

  dataInput <- reactive({            # <1>
    switch(input$dataset,
           rock = rock,
           pressure = pressure,
           cars = cars)
  })

  output$graph <- renderPlot({
    data <- dataInput()              # <2>
    plot(data[, 1:2])
  })

  output$summary <- renderPrint({
    data <- dataInput()              # <2>
    summary(data[, 1:2])
  })
}
```
1. Write the recipe **once**. It reads `input$dataset`, so it reacts to it
2. **Call** it, like a function: `dataInput()`, with the parentheses

```{shinylive-r}
#| standalone: true
#| components: [editor, viewer]
#| layout: vertical
#| viewerHeight: 650
## file: ui.R
{{< include ../apps/03-reactive/ui.R >}}
## file: server.R
{{< include ../apps/03-reactive/server.R >}}
```

Now the chain of reactions is:

```{mermaid}
flowchart LR
    I["input$dataset"] --> D["dataInput()"]
    D --> G["output$graph"]
    D --> S["output$summary"]
    style I fill:#2b6c8e,color:#fff
    style D fill:#f0ad4e,color:#fff
    style G fill:#8fd36f,color:#fff
    style S fill:#8fd36f,color:#fff
```

When `input$dataset` changes, `dataInput()` is recomputed **once**, and both outputs use the new value. If nothing changed, calling `dataInput()` again just returns the value already computed (Shiny *caches* it).

::: {.callout-warning}
## Three things to remember about `reactive()`

1. **Parentheses**: `dataInput()` is the value, `dataInput` (without parentheses) is the recipe itself. `plot(dataInput[, 1:2])` is an error
2. A reactive expression can only be **called inside reactive code** (`render*()`, another `reactive()`…), exactly like `input$...`
3. It is **lazy**: it runs only if some output needs it
:::

## Only what depends on a change re-runs

Shiny knows exactly who reads what. In this app each output prints the time it was last computed. Move the slider: which outputs are recomputed? And when you change the dataset?

```{shinylive-r}
#| standalone: true
#| components: [editor, viewer]
#| layout: vertical
#| viewerHeight: 560
## file: ui.R
library(shiny)

ui <- fluidPage(
  sidebarLayout(
    sidebarPanel(
      selectInput("dataset", "Choose a dataset:",
                  choices = c("rock", "pressure", "cars")),
      sliderInput("n", "Rows to show:", min = 1, max = 10, value = 3)
    ),
    mainPanel(
      h4("Summary (uses only the dataset)"),
      verbatimTextOutput("summary"),
      h4("First rows (uses the dataset AND the slider)"),
      verbatimTextOutput("rows")
    )
  )
)
## file: server.R
library(shiny)

now <- function() format(Sys.time(), "%H:%M:%OS2")

server <- function(input, output, session) {

  dataInput <- reactive({
    get(input$dataset)
  })

  output$summary <- renderPrint({
    cat("computed at", now(), "\n\n")
    summary(dataInput())
  })

  output$rows <- renderPrint({
    cat("computed at", now(), "\n\n")
    head(dataInput(), input$n)
  })
}
```

```{mermaid}
flowchart LR
    I["input$dataset"] --> D["dataInput()"]
    D --> S["output$summary"]
    D --> R["output$rows"]
    N["input$n"] --> R
    style I fill:#2b6c8e,color:#fff
    style N fill:#2b6c8e,color:#fff
    style D fill:#f0ad4e,color:#fff
    style S fill:#8fd36f,color:#fff
    style R fill:#8fd36f,color:#fff
```

The slider only touches `output$rows`; the dataset touches everything that depends on `dataInput()`.

## Exercise 1 · In your project

In your project (the `02-datasets` app), replace the two `switch()` with a single `reactive()` called `dataInput`, and use `dataInput()` in both outputs.

Then add a third output: a `tableOutput("head")` showing `head(dataInput())`.
:::

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## Solution 1

The server is the one of [`apps/03-reactive`](https://github.com/ottaviae/stat-shiny/tree/main/apps/03-reactive), plus:

```r
output$head <- renderTable({
  head(dataInput())
})
```

and in `ui.R`, inside `mainPanel()`: `tableOutput("head")` (remember the comma before it!).
:::
